content.text: I found the first material defect: every sitemap URL except the homepage redirects to a trailing-slash URL, but Twyne’s canonical tag strips that slash and points back to the redirecting URL. Google can resolve redirects, but a sitemap that lists redirects plus canonicals that disagree with the served URL sends contradictory indexing signals site-wide. I’m checking whether that is the only blocker before changing the URL policy consistently.

content.text:
Yes—Twyne has a live sitemap at [twyne.love/sitemap.xml](https://twyne.love/sitemap.xml), but I found indexing defects and fixed them locally.

The fixes include:

- Sitemap, canonical tags, redirects, and internal links now agree on trailing-slash URLs.
- Blog and writer indexes are server-rendered so crawlers receive actual content and links without JavaScript.
- Missing writers/posts now return real `404` responses instead of indexable soft-404 pages.
- Writer pages receive content-specific titles and descriptions.
- Dynamic published posts remain automatically added to the sitemap.

Relevant changes are in [seo.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/utils/seo.ts), [sitemap.xml/index.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/routes/sitemap.xml/index.ts), and [published-metadata.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/utils/published-metadata.ts).

Verification passed:

- 9 focused tests
- TypeScript compilation
- Full production build and lint, with only two existing image-optimization warnings
- Built-server smoke checks confirmed canonical `200` pages, server-rendered blog discovery, and genuine `404` responses

Vet could not complete: normal mode lacks an Anthropic credential, and the local Codex-backed fallback stalled.

Two important boundaries remain:

1. These edits are not deployed yet.
2. Production currently has zero published blog posts or writer pieces, so the sitemap contains only eight static pages. Technical SEO helps discovery, but substantive public articles and relevant external links are still necessary—especially because “Twyne” competes with several similarly named products.

After deployment, add `https://twyne.love/sitemap.xml` in Google Search Console and use URL Inspection → Test Live URL → Request Indexing for the homepage, docs, pricing, and the first substantive article. Google explicitly recommends canonical URLs in sitemaps and warns against conflicting sitemap/canonical signals; sitemap submission is a discovery hint, not an indexing guarantee. [Google canonical guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls), [Search Console sitemap submission](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7451001), [URL Inspection](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/9012289).

For Bing and other participating engines, submit the same sitemap in Bing Webmaster Tools; Bing currently recommends IndexNow for automated publication notifications. [Bing sitemap guidance](https://www.bing.com/webmasters/help/sitemaps-3b5cf6ed), [Bing URL submission](https://www.bing.com/webmasters/help/URL-Submission-62f2860b).
